answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. Each agent must solve non-parallelizable sequential puzzles broadcast by a network lantern, recording solutions onto an immutable basalt ledger. This forces attackers to commit scarce single-threaded processor time per identity rather than spawning a cheap plume of virtual clones. However, adversaries with custom low-latency ASICs can evaluate steps faster and maintain multiple identities.
